text: On scrutiny of the case papers our panel doctor opined that the patient's vitals were stable throughout the stay and the line of treatment given (oral medication and IV fluids) did not require admission. Hence the claim stands repudiated.
Knee arthroscopy was planned without any trial of physiotherapy or analgesics being on record. The surgery is therefore considered premature and not medically justified at this time.
The length of stay of 9 days is not supported by the clinical notes; the patient was fit for discharge on day 3. Expenses beyond day 3 are disallowed as not medically necessary.
The MRI and repeat blood tests were ordered without clinical indication and the admission appears to have been for evaluation of vague symptoms that could be done in OPD.
As per the medical opinion obtained by us, the procedure undertaken is not the standard of care for this diagnosis and a less invasive option was available.

The hospital records mention that the insured is a known case of diabetes for the last 6 years. The policy started 14 months ago, and diabetes-related complications are payable only after 36 months of continuous cover.
Cataract surgery has a two-year waiting period under the policy, and the admission took place in the first policy year.
The illness began 12 days after the policy start date and is not the result of an accident, so it falls in the initial waiting period.
The thyroid disorder was treated by Dr. Rao in 2019, well before you took this policy, and this history was not mentioned in the proposal form.
Hernia repair is a listed procedure that becomes payable only after 24 months of continuous coverage; the policy is in its second month.
The admission was for treatment of injuries sustained while under the influence of alcohol, which the policy does not pay for.
Rhinoplasty performed to improve appearance is not payable as it is a cosmetic procedure under the general exclusions.
The injury was suffered during a paragliding activity. Expenses arising from hazardous sports are outside the scope of cover.
IVF and other assisted reproduction treatments are specifically excluded from this policy.
Spectacles and the LASIK correction of refractive error of minus 3 dioptres are not covered in terms of the exclusion list.
The insured opted for a deluxe room at Rs 9,500 per day against the eligible limit of Rs 5,000 per day, so all associated charges have been reduced proportionately.
Only Rs 25,000 is payable for cataract per eye under the policy, and the balance of the bill is not admissible.
The entire sum insured of Rs 3 lakh and the cumulative bonus were used up by the hospitalization in March, so no balance is available for this claim.
Being a senior citizen policy, 20% of the admissible amount is borne by the insured. The settlement has been made after this deduction.
Charges for gloves, masks, diapers and food are listed as non-payable items and have been deducted from the bill.
We had asked for the original discharge summary and the histopathology report on 12/03/2024 and again on 28/03/2024. These are still pending, so the claim cannot be processed.
The date of admission on the hospital bill is 05/06/2024 but the discharge summary shows 07/06/2024; please clarify the discrepancy with supporting records.
The pharmacy bills were submitted without the doctor's prescription and batch numbers, and the claim form is not signed by the treating doctor.
As the claim exceeds Rs 1 lakh, the KYC documents of the proposer are mandatory. They have not been furnished despite reminders.
The X-ray films and the operative notes for the fracture surgery were not attached with the reimbursement file.
The reimbursement documents reached us 74 days after discharge, whereas the policy requires submission within 30 days. No reason for the delay has been given.
The planned surgery was not notified to us 48 hours before admission as required, and the hospital is not part of our network.
A claim for the same hospitalisation has already been paid under claim number CLM-2024-1187, so this second request cannot be entertained.
The hospital where treatment was taken has been removed from our panel for billing irregularities, and claims from it are not settled.
The insured holds another health policy with a different company that was not declared at the time of the claim.
The policy expired on 31/12/2023 and was renewed only on 15/02/2024. The hospitalisation on 20/01/2024 falls in the period when no cover was in force.
Your son is 27 years old, and dependent children are covered only up to the age of 25 under this plan.
The treatment was taken in Dubai. The policy covers treatment taken within India only.
Our investigation found that the bills were fabricated and the patient was never admitted to the hospital. The policy is being cancelled with forfeiture of premium.
The person treated is the insured's mother, who is not named in the policy schedule as a covered member.
